explanation.surface: A vintage motor, one of a fleet sent out by a hometown celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local star' sounds like a neighbourhood celebrity, but it is the star closest to us. Sunbeam was a British car manufacturer, active until the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunbeam was a British car marque, and a ray of light emitted by the Sun is one of countless such rays.

clue.text: Daughter leaves knotty loop in rope

indicators.note: whoever leaves is no longer there, so a letter disappears

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
nodose means having knots or knobs

explanation.surface: A daughter walks away from a tangled loop of rope.
explanation.walkthrough: Nodose is a rare botanical word for knotty or knobbly; taking out its D leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop with a running knot that tightens when pulled, made at the end of a cord.

clue.text: Glossy material from head of news area

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of news
an acre is a unit of area

explanation.surface: A glossy magazine's material comes from the editor of a local news region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glossy' hints at a magazine, but here it simply describes a shiny substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is mother-of-pearl, the iridescent lining of shells, a lustrous and shiny substance.

clue.text: Stick around with Heather

blocks.note: c is short for circa, Latin for around, used with dates
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: Hang around with Heather, as a friend might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick around' looks like one phrase, but 'Stick' is the definition and 'around' starts the wordplay. The capital H disguises the plant as a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to adhere closely or hold tightly to something, so it means to stick.

clue.text: Set of nine English notes repaid regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
nn is the abbreviation for notes, as pp is for pages
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Nine English banknotes are paid back at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' suggests banknotes or musical notes, but it is the scholarly abbreviation for notes, as in footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennead comes from the Greek for nine and names any group of nine, such as the nine Egyptian gods.

clue.text: During beating, writer settled for paying too much

indicators.note: something during an event happens inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: overcoming an opponent is beating them
a pen is a writing instrument
sat means settled into a seat

explanation.surface: While being thrashed, an author agreed to an overpriced settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but it is the instrument that writes. Two pieces go inside the beating word, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcompensate is to give more than is due to make up for something, literally paying out in excess.

clue.text: Go round to dispose of deal

indicators.note: to go round something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: to have a go is to have a try
to dispose of a meal is to eat it

explanation.surface: Pass round the cards in order to get rid of a bad hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go round' looks like one phrasal verb, but 'Go' is the noun meaning an attempt and 'round' the instruction to wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between nations, so it is a deal or pact.

clue.text: Perhaps bowler owned equipment to conserve energy

indicators.note: to conserve something is to keep it safe inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: had means owned
E is the symbol for energy
gear is equipment

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler might have kit to save his strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' suggests cricket, but it is the hat; 'Perhaps' marks it as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler hat is one example of something worn on the head, so the general category fits.

clue.text: Head of engineering impressed by modest digital skill

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so only the first letter is kept
to be impressed by is to be pressed into, so one piece is pushed inside another

blocks.note: slight means small or modest
the first letter of engineering

explanation.surface: An engineering boss is impressed by someone's modest computer skills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests computers, but it refers to the fingers, as in sleight of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is dexterity, especially manual trickery, and fingers are digits, so it is a skill of the fingers.
